presentation.title: One local ledger for the whole creator campaign
presentation.body: UGC CLI keeps the record of creator work in one local SQLite file you own: campaigns, versioned briefs, creator profiles and identities, assignments, shipments, messages, submissions, content-addressed assets, usage-rights grants, payment records, publications and attribution, over an immutable audit log. It needs no marketplace account, no hosted database and no payment provider.

presentation.title: A record of the work, not the execution of it
presentation.body: Commissioning the creator work itself is HandToHuman's ugc_video task; this CLI is the ledger beside it, holding the campaign, rights, asset, payment-record and publication history. Nothing in this walkthrough contacts a creator. A payment row is recorded compensation state, not settlement, and moves no money. Publication fails closed without an approved brief, a reviewed submission and valid rights scope.

presentation.title: Open the ledger you are going to keep
presentation.body: The ledger is the SQLite file --db points at, created on first use with owner-only permissions and asked for a count of every record kind it holds. Point --db at a scratch file to rehearse the journey, or at your working ledger to start for real. This step is satisfied once your own ledger opens and reports those counts.

presentation.title: Import your existing ledger or record the first campaign
presentation.body: If you already use UGC CLI, run this walkthrough with --import and the JSON written by `ugc-cli standalone export`; the ledger validates every record and relationship before one transaction preserves campaign, brief, creator, rights, and payment metadata. Existing identical records remain unchanged, any difference or unsupported record refuses the whole import, and no commission, outreach, payment, or publication runs. If you have no export, create a campaign with real working details. This step completes only after the destination reads an accepted campaign back by id.
